en: While exiled in Dapitan, Jose Rizal sculpted a marble statue titled 'The Triumph of Science over Death'.
The first official Philippine flag was hand-sewn by Marcela Agoncillo and her helpers in Hong Kong.
The Philippine President can only declare martial law for a maximum of sixty days without congressional approval.
The Philippine flag is uniquely flown with the red stripe on top to indicate a state of war.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate their houses with kiping, which are colorful, leaf-shaped rice wafers.
The indigenous Ifugao people carved the massive Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over two thousand years ago.
The ancient Baybayin writing system uses exactly seventeen characters, consisting of three vowels and fourteen consonants.
The original Filipino tradition of bayanihan involved an entire community physically carrying a nipa hut to a new location.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift bamboo incubator powered by a hot water bottle for premature babies.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the Bonifacio Monument featuring sixteen figures representing the first provinces that revolted against Spain.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution guarantees every citizen the specific right to a balanced and healthful ecology.
Filipino women won the right to vote in 1937 after a special plebiscite with over four hundred thousand participants.
